text:
Recent work supports separating recency from order sensitivity. “Does It Look Sequential?” (RecSys 2024) uses interaction shuffling across 15 datasets and finds several popular benchmarks weakly sequential; its authors’ implementation includes GRU4Rec, prediction-overlap measures and bootstrap comparisons. The 2026 extension explicitly distinguishes recency-based from order-sensitive patterns. These results motivate preserving the recent suffix while perturbing older interactions, rather than interpreting unrestricted shuffle damage as evidence for long-range dependencies. [2024 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [implementation](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential/), [2026 extension](https://publications.hse.ru/en/articles/1122974633).

Supervision and target construction are separate confounders: recency-sampling research changes which interactions become training targets, including for GRU4Rec; “Time to Split” (2025) shows why target selection and evaluation horizons require explicit specification. Neither establishes that prefix removal itself improves GRU4Rec. [Recency sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), [Time to Split](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748164).

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: freeze each category’s single trained GRU and pair identical validation users, targets and candidate sets. Compare full history with suffix-only input, equal-length windows at different recencies, and prefix shuffles retaining the same recent suffix. Measure target-rank change alongside final-hidden-state distance and target-versus-negative score margins; hidden-state movement alone does not establish harmful context. Report paired user-bootstrap intervals, history-length strata and category-macro HR@10 changes. Verify padding invariance by skipping padded recurrent updates and reading the final nonpadding position. For subsequent training comparisons, match target identities, supervision counts and update budgets. These are proposed controls, not a published validated diagnostic suite.
